section: Environmental legislation in India - Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981, Environment (Protection) Act 1986

accepted.s: Which combination correctly identifies the FIRST and the LATEST laws in India’s pollution-control legislative sequence mentioned below?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 and Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
accepted.x: The Water Act of 1974 is regarded as India’s first pollution-control law, while the National Green Tribunal Act of 2010 is the latest in the stated legislative chain.
accepted.tq: Use the first-and-last method to identify the chronological extremes.

accepted.s: Under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), the target is to reduce PM10 concentration by up to what percentage in 130 cities by 2025–26, compared with the 2019–20 baseline?
accepted.x: NCAP targets an improvement of up to 40% in PM10 concentration by 2025–26 in 130 cities, using 2019–20 as the baseline year.
accepted.tq: Match the target percentage with the specified year and number of cities.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB):
1. It was established in 1976 under the Water Act.
2. It enforces the Water Act, Air Act and Environment (Protection) Act, along with waste-management rules.
3. It issues siting guidelines for industries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. APPCB was established in 1976 under the Water Act, enforces the major environmental laws and waste rules, and provides industrial siting guidelines.
accepted.tq: Check whether the statements cover the board’s establishment, enforcement role and regulatory guidance.

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was established in which year?
accepted.x: The APPCB was set up in 1976 under the Water Act.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related years associated with environmental institutions and laws.

accepted.s: Which one of the following preceded the Air Act in the stated institutional sequence of environmental regulation in India?
o: Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board
Environmental Protection Fund
National Green Tribunal
Central Pollution Control Board
accepted.x: The Central Pollution Control Board was established in 1974, before the enactment of the Air Act. The APPCB was established later, in 1976.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution that came earlier by separating the central and State-level pollution-control bodies.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about recent environmental developments:
1. The Vanashakti ruling concerned ex post facto environmental clearances.
2. The National Green Tribunal issued a suo motu notice to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh regarding sewage in drinking water.
3. An integrated-consent reform involving indefinite validity of the Consent to Operate was reported in January 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Vanashakti ruling dealt with ex post facto clearances, the NGT notice concerned sewage contamination of drinking water in three States, and integrated consent with indefinite CTO validity was a reported January 2026 development.
accepted.tq: Verify each statement against the distinct case, tribunal action and regulatory reform before selecting the combined code.

accepted.s: A State administration seeks to accelerate environmental clearances while improving coordination among departments under the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP). Which approach is associated with Andhra Pradesh in this context?
o: Using digitisation and a single-window system for clearances
Transferring all environmental powers to local bodies
Restricting industrial clearances to manual applications
Replacing pollution-control laws with voluntary guidelines
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh streamlined clearances through digitisation and a single-window mechanism under BRAP.
accepted.tq: Translate the administrative objective into the specific institutional reform associated with the State.

accepted.s: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 are best classified as which of the following?
o: A programme for reducing PM10 in 130 cities
A State pollution-control board established under the Water Act
A judicial ruling on ex post facto clearances
A recent environmental regulatory development in India
accepted.x: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 constitute a recent environmental regulatory development. The other options refer respectively to the Vanashakti ruling, NCAP and APPCB.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a new set of Rules from a judicial ruling, a pollution-control programme and a regulatory board.
